text: C2 holds up a picture frame with ‘Scene 1’ on the back
speaker: C2

text: Scene 1
speaker: C2

text: C2 turns the frame round to reveal a picture of Basil’s Studio and hangs on the wall
speaker: C2

text: Basil Hallward’s Studio.
speaker: C1/3

text: Lord Henry Wotton sat on the corner of the Divan (dress and bring Henry forward).
speaker: C1

text: In the centre of the room, clamped to an upright easel, stood the full-length portrait of a young man of extraordinary personal beauty (Dorian is dressed and brought to stand behind frame).
speaker: C2

text: and in front of it, some little distance away, was sitting the artist himself, Basil Hallward (Basil is dressed and brought forward and sat in front of picture).
speaker: C3

text: (gets up and stands looking at picture) It is your best work, Basil, the best thing you have ever done. You must certainly exhibit it at the Grosvenor.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: I don't think I shall send it anywhere.
speaker: Basil

text: (stretches out again) My dear fellow, why? What odd chaps you painters are! You do anything in the world to gain a reputation. As soon as you have one, you seem to want to throw it away.
speaker: Lord H

text: I know you will laugh at me but I really can't exhibit it. I have put too much of myself into it. (Lord H laughs)
speaker: Basil

text: Who is the young Adonis?
speaker: Lord H

text: Dorian Gray.
speaker: Basil

text: So explain to me why you won’t exhibit his picture.
speaker: Lord H

text: Harry, every portrait that is painted with feeling is a portrait of the artist. It is not the sitter who is revealed by the painter; it is rather the painter who reveals himself. I am afraid that I have shown in this picture the secret of my own soul. (covers it)
speaker: Basil

text: And what is that?
speaker: Lord H

text: Two months ago I went to a crush at Lady Brandon's.
speaker: Basil

text: C1, C2, C3 become guests. Dorian goes one side of them, Basil the other.
speaker: Stage

text: I suddenly became conscious that someone was looking at me. I turned and saw Dorian Gray for the first time. When our eyes met a curious sensation of terror came over me. I knew I’d come face to face with someone would absorb my whole nature, my whole soul, my very art itself. I was afraid and turned to quit the room. I stumbled against Lady Brandon.
speaker: Basil

text: You are not going to run away so soon, Mr. Hallward?
speaker: Lady B (C3)

text: I could not get rid of her.
speaker: Basil

text: Basil, Lady B, C1 & C2 & Dorian enact the following:
speaker: Stage

text: She brought him up to royalties,
speaker: C1

text: and people with stars and garters,
speaker: C2

text: and elderly ladies with gigantic tiaras and parrot noses.
speaker: C1

text: She spoke of me as her dearest friend.
speaker: Basil

text: My dear friend Basil
speaker: Lady B

text: Although I had only met her once before. Suddenly I found myself face to face with the young man. Our eyes met again. It was reckless of me, but I asked Lady Brandon to introduce me to him.
speaker: Basil

text: Charming boy. Poor dear mother and I absolutely inseparable. Quite forget what he does. Afraid he doesn't do anything - oh, yes, plays the piano - or is it the violin, dear Mr.Gray?
speaker: Lady B

text: Neither of us could help laughing, and we became friends at once.
speaker: Basil

text: (chorus to back)
speaker: Stage

text: Laughter is not at all a bad beginning for a friendship, and it is far the best ending for one.
speaker: Lord H

text: I couldn't be happy if I didn't see him every day. He is absolutely necessary to me.
speaker: Basil

text: I thought you would never care for anything but your art, so tell me dear Basil why won’t you exhibit his portrait?
speaker: Lord H

text: There is too much of myself in the thing, Harry - too much of myself! He shall never know anything about it. But the world might guess it, and I will not bare my soul to their shallow prying eyes.
speaker: Basil

text: Tell me, is Dorian Gray very fond of you?
speaker: Lord H

text: Mostly, he is charming to me, but sometimes he seems to delight in giving me pain. Then I feel that I have given away my whole soul.
speaker: Basil

text: Days in summer, Basil, are apt to linger, perhaps you will tire sooner than he will.
speaker: Lord H

text: Harry, don't talk like that. As long as I live, the personality of Dorian Gray will dominate me.
speaker: Basil

text: Those who are faithful know only the trivial side of love: it is the faithless who know love's tragedies. Now I have stayed long enough to miss a dreadful luncheon with my Aunt where the conversation would have been about feeding the poor (he snaps his fingers) My dear fellow, I have just remembered where I heard the name of Dorian Gray.
speaker: Lord H

text: Where? Where was it?
speaker: Basil

text: It was at my aunt, Lady Agatha's.
speaker: Lord H

text: I have discovered a wonderful young man. He is going to help me in the East End. His name is Dorian Gray. He has a very earnest and beautiful nature. (during this gets ready to be greasy young man)
speaker: C2 as Lady A

text: I at once pictured to myself a creature with spectacles and lank hair, horribly freckled, and tramping about on huge feet. I wish I had known it was your friend.
speaker: Lord H

text: I am very glad you didn't, Harry.
speaker: Basil

text: Why?
speaker: Lord H

text: I don't want you to meet him.
speaker: Basil

text: Mr. Dorian Gray sir.
speaker: Butler (C3)

text: Well Basil you’ll have to introduce me now.
speaker: Lord H

text: Show Mr. Gray in, Parker.
speaker: Basil

text: Yes sir.
speaker: Butler

text: Butler prepares Dorian – gives him the piano music.
speaker: Stage

text: Dorian Gray is my dearest friend. He has a simple and a beautiful nature. Don't spoil him. Don't try to influence him. Your influence would be bad.  Don't take away from me the one person who gives to my art whatever charm it possesses. Mind, Harry, I trust you.
speaker: Basil

text: What nonsense you talk!
speaker: Lord H

text: Dorian enters with piano music
speaker: Stage

text: Forest Scenes - You must lend me these, Basil, I want to learn them. They are perfectly charming.
speaker: Dorian

text: That entirely depends on how you sit today, Dorian.
speaker: Basil

text: Oh, I am tired of sitting, and I don't want a life-sized portrait of myself. (he sees Lord H) I beg your pardon, Basil, but I didn't know you had any one with you.
speaker: Dorian

text: This is Lord Henry Wotton, an old Oxford friend of mine. (Lord H extends hand and Dorian crosses) I have just been telling him what a capital sitter you were, and now you have spoiled everything.
speaker: Basil

text: You have not spoiled my pleasure in meeting you, Mr. Gray, My aunt has often spoken to me about you.  You are one of her favourites, and, I am afraid, one of her victims also.
speaker: Lord H

text: I am in Lady Agatha's bad books at present. I promised to go to a club in Whitechapel with her last Tuesday, and I really forgot all about it.  We were to have played a duet together - I don't know what she will say to me.
speaker: Dorian

text: I don't think it really matters about your not being there.  The audience probably thought it was a duet.  When Aunt Agatha sits down to the piano, she makes quite enough noise for two people.
speaker: Lord H

text: (laughs) That is very horrid to her, and not very nice to me.
speaker: Dorian

text: You are too charming to go in for philanthropy, Mr. Gray - far too charming. (He lies on the divan)
speaker: Lord H

text: Harry, I want to finish this picture to-day. Would you think it awfully rude of me if I asked you to go away?
speaker: Basil

text: Basil turns painting to face US and uncovers it
speaker: Stage

text: Am I to go, Mr. Gray?
speaker: Lord H

text: Oh, please don't, Lord Henry. Basil if Lord Henry goes, I shall go too.  You never open your lips while you are painting, and it is horribly dull standing on a platform. Ask him to stay.  I insist upon it.
speaker: Dorian

text: If Dorian wishes it, of course you must stay, Harry. Stay, to oblige Dorian, and to oblige me (gazing at the picture) And now, Dorian, get up on the platform, and don't pay any attention to what Lord Henry says.  He has a very bad influence over all his friends, with the single exception of myself.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian takes up a pose and Basil begins to paint - glances between Lord H and Dorian
speaker: Stage

text: Have you really a very bad influence, Lord Henry?  As bad as Basil says?
speaker: Dorian

text: There is no such thing as a good influence, Mr.Gray.  All influence is immoral - immoral from the scientific point of view.
speaker: Lord H

text: Why?
speaker: Dorian

text: Because to influence a person is to give him one's own soul.  He does not think his natural thoughts, or burn with his natural passions. His virtues are not real to him.  His sins, if there are such things as sins, are borrowed. People are afraid of themselves, nowadays. They have forgotten the highest of all duties, the duty that one owes to one's self.
speaker: Lord H

text: Just turn your head a little more to the left, Dorian, like a good boy.
speaker: Basil

text: Every impulse that we strive to strangle broods in the mind and poisons us. The only way to get rid of a temptation is to yield to it. Resist it, and your soul grows sick with longing for the things it has forbidden to itself, with desire for what its monstrous laws have made monstrous and unlawful. You, Mr. Gray, you yourself, with your rose-red youth and your rose-white boyhood, you have had passions that have made you afraid, thoughts that have filled you with terror, day-dreams and sleeping dreams whose mere memory might stain your cheek with shame…
speaker: Lord H

text: Stop! you bewilder me.  I don't know what to say.  There is some answer to you, but I cannot find it.  Don’t speak.  Let me think.  Or, rather, let me try not to think.
speaker: Dorian

text: For nearly ten minutes he stood there, motionless, with parted lips and eyes strangely bright. The few words that Basil's friend had said to him had touched some secret chord that had never been touched before.
speaker: C1

text: Words! Mere words! How terrible they were! How clear, and vivid, and cruel! One could not escape from them. And yet what a subtle magic there was in them! Mere words! Was there anything so real as words?
speaker: C2

text: Yes; there had been things in his boyhood that he had not understood. He understood them now. Life suddenly became fiery-coloured to him. It seemed to him that he had been walking in fire. Why had he not known it?
speaker: C3

text: With his subtle smile, Lord Henry watched him. He knew when to say nothing. He was amazed at the sudden impression that his words had produced.  He remembered a book that he had read when he was sixteen, which had revealed to him much that he had not known before.
speaker: C2 (with Lord H)

text: C2 gives Lord H the book, with a smile.  Lord H looks at it and puts it inside his jacket.
speaker: Stage

text: Was Dorian Gray passing through a similar experience?
speaker: C2

text: Hallward painted away with that marvellous bold touch of his. He was unconscious of the silence.
speaker: C3 (with Basil)

text: I don't know what Harry has been saying to you, but he has certainly made you have the most wonderful expression. I have caught the effect I wanted - the half-parted lips and the bright look in the eyes.  I suppose he has been paying you compliments.  You mustn't believe a word that he says.
speaker: Basil

text: He has certainly not been paying me compliments.  Perhaps that is the reason that I don't believe anything he has told me.
speaker: Dorian

text: You know you believe it all (they exchange looks) Sit with me, Dorian
speaker: Lord H

text: Dorian sits next to Lord H on the Divan
speaker: Stage

text: Don't keep Dorian too long.  I have never been in better form for painting than I am today.
speaker: Basil

text: You are a wonderful creation.  You know more than you think you know, just as you know less than you want to know. (Dorian turns away slightly unsure) You have the most marvellous youth, and youth is the one thing worth having.
speaker: Lord H

text: I don't feel that, Lord Henry.
speaker: Dorian

text: No, you don't feel it now.  Some day, when you are old and wrinkled and ugly, when thought has seared your forehead with its lines, and passion branded your lips with its hideous fires, you will feel it, you will feel it terribly.  You have a wonderfully beautiful face, Mr. Gray, but time is jealous of you. You will become sallow, and hollow-cheeked, and dull-eyed.  Live the wonderful life that is in you!  Let nothing be lost upon you.  Be always searching for new sensations.  Be afraid of nothing for there is such a little time that your youth will last - such a little time.
speaker: Lord H

text: I am waiting. The light is quite perfect.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian goes to move back to his pose.  Lord H’s words stop him
speaker: Stage

text: You are glad you have met me, Mr. Gray
speaker: Lord H

text: Yes, I am glad now.  I wonder shall I always be glad?
speaker: Dorian

text: (he resumes his pose - passage of time as Basil paints)
speaker: Stage

text: Tick tock, tick tock etc (as they move the hands of a big clock)
speaker: C1,2,3

text: It is quite finished.
speaker: Basil

text: Basil turns the painting, C2 with Dorian mask on, stands behind the frame
speaker: Stage

text: My dear fellow, I congratulate you most warmly. It is the finest portrait of modern times.  Mr. Gray, come over and look at yourself.
speaker: Lord H

text: Dorian looks at painting
speaker: Stage

text: The sense of his own beauty came on him like a revelation.
speaker: C2

text: He had never felt it before.
speaker: C1

text: Basil's compliments had seemed to him to be merely the charming exaggeration of friendship.
speaker: C3

text: He had listened to them, laughed at them, forgotten them.
speaker: C1

text: They had not influenced his nature.
speaker: C3

text: Then had come Lord Henry Wotton warning of the brevity of youth.
speaker: C1

text: That had stirred him at the time,
speaker: C1/3

text: Chorus (turn Dorian to front)
speaker: Stage

text: Yes, there will be a day when your face will be wrinkled and wizen, your eyes dim and colourless, the grace of your figure broken and deformed.
speaker: C1

text: The scarlet will pass away from your lips and the ebony steal from your hair.
speaker: C2

text: You will become dreadful, hideous, and uncouth.
speaker: C1/2/3

text: Don’t you like it?
speaker: Basil

text: It is one of the greatest things in modern art. I will give you anything you like to ask for it.  I must have it.
speaker: Lord H

text: It is not my property, Harry.
speaker: Basil

text: Whose property is it?
speaker: Lord H

text: Dorian’s, of course.
speaker: Basil

text: How sad it is! I shall grow old, and horrible, and dreadful.  But this picture will remain always young.  If it were only the other way!  If it were I who was to be always young, and the picture that was to grow old! For that - for that - I would give everything! I would give my soul for that!
speaker: Dorian

text: Soul soul soul
speaker: Chorus

text: You would hardly care for such an arrangement, Basil. It would be rather hard lines on your work.
speaker: Lord H

text: I should object very strongly, Harry.
speaker: Basil

text: I believe you would, Basil. You like your art better than your friends. How long will you like me? Till I have my first wrinkle, I suppose.  I know, now, that when one loses one's good looks, one loses everything. Your picture has taught me that.  Youth is the only thing worth having. When I find that I am growing old, I shall kill myself.
speaker: Dorian

text: Dorian! You are not jealous of material things, are you?
speaker: Basil

text: I am jealous of the portrait you have painted of me.  Why should it keep what I must lose? Why did you paint it?  It will mock me some day - mock me horribly!
speaker: Dorian

text: This is your doing, Harry
speaker: Basil

text: It is the real Dorian Gray — that is all.
speaker: Lord H

text: Between you both you have made me hate the finest piece of work I have ever done, and I will destroy it.
speaker: Basil

text: (he picks up a palette knife and moves towards the portrait)
speaker: Stage

text: Don't, Basil, don’t! It would be murder!
speaker: Dorian

text: I am glad you appreciate my work at last, Dorian.
speaker: Basil

text: Appreciate it?  I am in love with it, Basil.  It is part of myself.
speaker: Dorian

text: Well, as soon as you are dry, you shall be varnished, and framed, and sent home.  Then you can do what you like with yourself.
speaker: Basil

text: If I am not allowed the picture at least let me have your company. Let us go to the theatre to-night.
speaker: Lord H

text: I should like that
speaker: Dorian

text: And you will come, too, Basil, won't you?
speaker: Lord H

text: I can't, really.  I have a lot of work to do.
speaker: Basil

text: Well, then, you and I will go alone, Mr. Gray.
speaker: Lord H

text: I should like that awfully.
speaker: Dorian

text: I shall stay with the real Dorian.
speaker: Basil

text: C1 and 3 stand by portrait and caress frame
speaker: Stage

text: Is it the real Dorian? Am I really like that?
speaker: Dorian

text: Yes; you are just like that.
speaker: Basil

text: How wonderful, Basil!
speaker: Dorian

text: Don’t go to the theatre to-night, Dorian. Stop and dine with me.
speaker: Basil

text: I can't, Basil.
speaker: Dorian

text: Why?
speaker: Basil

text: Because I have promised Lord Henry to go with him.
speaker: Dorian

text: I entreat you.
speaker: Basil

text: Dorian hesitates, and looked over at Lord Henry, who gives an amused smile.
speaker: Stage

text: I must go, Basil.
speaker: Dorian

text: Very well. It is rather late, and, as you have to dress, you had better lose no time.  Good-bye, Harry.  Good-bye, Dorian.  Come and see me soon.  And ... Harry remember what I asked you this morning.
speaker: Basil

text: I have forgotten it.
speaker: Lord H

text: I trust you.
speaker: Basil

text: I wish I could trust myself. Good-bye, Basil.  It has been a most interesting afternoon.
speaker: Lord H

text: As the door closed behind them, the painter flung himself down upon the Divan, and a look of pain came into his face.
speaker: C1

text: Divan in place for next scene. Lose chair, picture and paint brushes
speaker: Stage
